hook: The shop says **"no refund"** on my faulty product.
hook_q: A shop refused to refund a defective product. What can I do?

slides.title: What counts as a **defect?**
slides.body: Any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard that the law or a contract requires, or that the trader claimed.

slides.title: Refusing a refund can be **unfair.**
slides.body: Refusing to take back defective goods and refund the price within the period stated in the bill, or within 30 days if none is stated, is an unfair trade practice.

slides.title: Always **ask for a bill.**
slides.body: Not issuing a bill, cash memo or receipt for goods sold is itself an unfair trade practice. Any return period stated on it is what the refund rule uses.

slides.title: First, try the **National Consumer Helpline.**
slides.body: Call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915 to register your grievance at the pre-litigation stage. The helpline works in 17 languages.

slides.title: Still stuck? **File a complaint.**
slides.body: You can complain when goods you bought have a defect, or a trader used an unfair trade practice. Complaints can be filed online on e-Jagriti, which now includes e-Daakhil.

slides.title: What the Commission **can order.**
list: Pay compensation for loss caused by the seller's negligence

Target if the goods need **analysis or testing**.

sources: Department of Consumer Affairs – National Consumer Helpline (PIB, Jan 2026)
caption:
Shop refusing to refund a faulty product? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ A defect is any fault or shortcoming in quality, quantity, purity or standard
2️⃣ Refusing to take back defective goods and refund within the period in the bill (or 30 days if none) is an unfair trade practice
3️⃣ Not giving a bill or cash memo is also an unfair trade practice
4️⃣ Try the National Consumer Helpline first: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915
5️⃣ Still stuck? File a consumer complaint, online on e-Jagriti
6️⃣ The Commission can order removal of the defect, replacement, a refund with interest, or compensation

Source: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sec 2(6), 2(10), 2(47), 38(7), 39); Dept of Consumer Affairs; PIB
